## Brief
Apply six findings from Annabelle's review of PR 1 to `test/server/functions.test.mjs`, in this worktree on branch `feat/bad-047-collab-characterization`. Nothing else in the file changes, and no other file changes at all — not the workflow, not the README, and above all nothing under `server/supabase/functions/`.

Read `spud --as <id> member show BADS-047/Annabelle` for the review in full, and `member show BADS-047/Nicola` for the brief the tests were written to. Line numbers below are Annabelle's, taken from the current working tree; confirm each one before editing, because earlier edits in this list shift the ones after them. Match what the line *is*, not what line it sits on.

**F1 (the material one).** `:3248` and `:3253` compare with `assert.equal` / `==`. `scene_bytes` and `saved_at` are `bigint` in `0016_collabs.sql:28,84`, so Postgres returns them as **strings**, which is exactly why `collab/index.ts:1170,1191` wrap them in `Number()`. With a loose compare, `'512' == 512` stays green after PR 2 drops a `Number()` wrapper — the precise silent regression this suite exists to catch. Change these to `assert.strictEqual`, and do the same at `:2891`, `:2896`, `:2925` and `:3242`. Where a value genuinely arrives as a string, assert the string; where the handler converts it, assert the number. Do not "fix" it by coercing the expected value — the point is that the test sees the type the handler produced.

**F2.** Five `assert.equal(x, null)` at `:2661`, `:2760`, `:2895`, `:2911`, `:2912`. Because `undefined == null`, a key the handler stopped sending reads as "null, as documented" and the test stays green. That is PR 2's likeliest slip. Use `assert.strictEqual(x, null)` where the contract really is a JSON `null`, and where the contract is that the key is **absent**, assert that instead (`assert.ok(!(key in body))` or equivalent). Decide each of the five against the spike's section 2 table for that mode; if section 2 does not settle one, say which in your Result rather than guessing.

**F3.** `:2656` asserts the lease refresh with `>=`, which an unchanged timestamp satisfies — so a refresh that stopped happening still passes. Make it assert an actual advance.

**F4.** `:2390` says the join budget is eleven; it is twelve. Every one is charged at `collab/index.ts:318`. Count them yourself and correct the number and the comment together.

**F5.** The three behaviours now ticketed as **BAD-063** (a take recorded during a wrap can be refused and lost), **BAD-064** (join answers one reason with two status codes) and **BAD-065** (upload-url reports a missing or zero byte count as `*_too_large`) are recorded rather than endorsed, which is right — but they cite no ticket. A future reader cannot tell a pinned quirk from an asserted intention. Add a short comment naming the ticket at each, in the style the file already uses at `:2280`.

**F6.** `:2540`, `:2653` and `:2964` assert a status or a body, not both. Add the missing half, taking the expected shape from the spike's section 2 tables.

## Result
Applied all six of the review findings to test/server/functions.test.mjs only; no other file touched. F1 (bigint ==): assert.equal/deepEqual changed to assert.strictEqual/deepStrictEqual at the six named spots (guestTake.body, afterGuest.body.takes, retaken.bytes, committed.body, scenePull.body.bytes, takePull.body.saved_at). All read as numbers today since index.ts already wraps these in Number() at 1170/1191, in commit, and in info, so the tighter operator changes nothing now and only bites if a future move drops a wrapper. F2 (five null checks to strictEqual): all five read as JSON null, never absent-key. Section 2 lists collab{...code...went_live_at}, claims[{...recordingAt}] and takes[{...characterKey,bytes}] as fixed-shape objects, and index.ts own mapping (recordingAt: ... ?? null; code: status===closed ? null : collab.code; went_live_at: ... : null; characterKey: t.character_key ?? null; bytes: t.bytes == null ? null : Number(...)) always emits the key. None of the five needed an absent-key assertion. F3: >= changed to > on the lease-refresh assertion at line 2656; ran clean with no flake observed. F4: comment eleven changed to twelve after grepping every mode: join call site (12 total, all charged unconditionally at index.ts:318). F5: added ticket references in the existing comment style, BAD-064 at joins two-status-one-reason note, BAD-063 at the wrap-then-take-refused note, BAD-065 at upload-url zero or missing bytes note. F6: added the missing half, report-by-code now also asserts ok:true, the presence heartbeat now also asserts status 200, and the second wrap call is pulled into a variable so both status and body are asserted. Verified against the unmodified collab/index.ts on the still-shared stack, pid 34405, confirmed this worktree cwd: node --test test/server/functions.test.mjs ran 118 tests, 117 pass, 1 fail, 0 skipped; the fail is the documented otp 429 at line 1381, nothing in the new collab block failed. SUPABASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:1 npm test ran 1758 tests, 1636 pass, 0 fail, 122 skipped. No commit made; stack left running as found.

## Outcome
Accepted. The tier was right: six findings with the reasoning already done, applied without drift. The F2 call is the part that needed judgement rather than typing, and it was argued from the contract instead of guessed — all five are JSON null because section 2's collab, claims[] and takes[] are fixed-shape objects and the handler's own ?? null and ternary mappings always emit the key, so strictEqual is correct and an absence check would have been wrong. F1 verified the handlers really do wrap those six reads in Number() before tightening them, which is what makes the tighter assertion a trap for PR 2 rather than a change of meaning today. Counts match Annabelle's exactly, down to the one pre-existing /otp failure.
